detail.body:
Main already supports FP8 parameter gather, including the initialization and synchronization fixes from #6754. This PR refactors Muon FP8 staging and makes Adam sharding independent of the Muon layout. The branch is rebased onto main `e30d863a6`.

## Scope

Both layouts reuse main's existing `ChainedOptimizer(LayerWise(Muon), DistributedOptimizer(Adam))` construction:

| Parameter owner | Compact layout | Padded layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Muon | Whole-parameter ownership, unpadded buffers, all-reduce gradients | Existing shard-aligned layout and reduce-scatter |
| Adam | Standard DistOpt sharding and reduce-scatter | Standard DistOpt sharding and reduce-scatter |

Only compact Muon buffers receive a private `dataclasses.replace(ddp_config, use_distributed_optimizer=False)` configuration. Adam retains `True`; the shared configuration is not changed to disable DistOpt. Training wrappers and direct core DDP construction use the same layout functions.

One `uses_grad_buffer_for_fp8_param_gather(param, ddp_config)` predicate defines staging independently of layout and tensor-parallel sharding:

| Parameter | Gradient-buffer reuse |
| --- | --- |
| Gather disabled, or high-precision parameter | Never |
| Plain/grouped MXFP8, either optimizer owner | Existing `--reuse-grad-buf-for-mxfp8-param-ag` flag |
| Muon blockwise FP8 | BF16 staging |
| Adam blockwise FP8 | Never; native FP8 DistOpt gather in both layouts |

No reuse flag is added, renamed or deprecated. Compact Muon transport supports plain MXFP8 and blockwise tensors; existing explicit errors cover generic Float8Tensor, NVFP4 and GroupedTensor. Grouped-MXFP8 eligibility in the general predicate does not imply compact Muon transport support. The compact MXFP8 opt-in guard does not restrict ordinary BF16 parameters.

The refactor keeps TE publication/quantization separate from transport staging, handles owner and non-owner publication after gather, and retains main's relocated-parameter copyback. GDP uses the existing `ensure_params_ready` helper before direct convolution-weight reads or CP weight slicing. Explicit refresh waits for pending gather; `zero_grad_buffer()` remains identical to main.

Checkpoint production methods and the optimizer-chain implementation are unchanged. The existing expert-Adam assertion is retained. Moving compact Adam to DistOpt changes optimizer ownership relative to main's compact path; validation covers new checkpoints saved and resumed with the same layout and topology, not migration from the old compact optimizer container.

## Relationship to related work

| Already in main | Remaining work in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| #6754: high-precision initialization and FP8 synchronization fixes | Muon staging and publication for both layouts |
| Native DistOpt Adam blockwise gather | Preserve native transport while centralizing the reuse policy |
| Padded LayerWise/Muon plus Adam DistOpt composition | Reuse that composition for compact Muon |
| Existing checkpoint implementations | Exercise same-version save/load without changing those implementations |

Applicable work from Zhongbo's [full branch](https://github.com/zhongbozhu/Megatron-LM/commit/8291af60c756bedecc0518807df48152140db482), [1/2](https://github.com/zhongbozhu/Megatron-LM/commit/3f611b0c00c64c755ed2e5c88751eca5e1a0184a) and [2/2](https://github.com/zhongbozhu/Megatron-LM/commit/87f63035ec6f5d81c44a1e8c72a7bee2d3c3f906) is incorporated here. #4987 is historical context. Duplicate main changes and the decoupled-layout toggle are removed. General DistOpt CLI cleanup, expert-Adam routing extensions and empty-padding-bucket checkpoint fixes remain outside this PR.

## Validation

GPU-tested code: `238b019b9`. Final head `1f8ab6a10` only clarifies two docstrings; executable Python ASTs are unchanged. Syntax, Black, isort, Ruff and diff checks passed. Local Claude CLI review of the implementation found no actionable introduced defects.

### Unit comparisons

**370 selected logical unit cases passed, zero failed/skipped**, with **4 ranks** on head `238b019b9`. The comparisons are:

| Check | Comparison / assertion |
| --- | --- |
| Adam ownership and buffer routing | Adam FP32 master shards contain each element exactly once across DP; compact Muon has one whole-parameter owner, no padding and all-reduce; Adam retains DistOpt/reduce-scatter. Both training wrappers and direct core construction are covered. The expert-Adam assertion remains. |
| Reuse policy and type boundaries | Gather/layout/TP/owner/recipe/old-flag matrix; high-precision parameters never reuse; Adam blockwise stays native FP8. Real TE negative tests cover unsupported compact tensor types. |
| Dense/MoE numerical parity | Within each recipe and layout, gather ON/OFF: 30-step loss, outputs, gradient snapshots, FP32 masters and high-precision forward weights compare exactly. Covers layout/overlap ON/OFF and expert-DP=1/>1. Clipping is disabled in this isolation test (the end-to-end runs use clip=1). No per-step force-sync; diagnostic snapshots still perform extra GPU reads/collectives. |
| GDP AdamW + MoE Muon | Within each recipe, layout × overlap ON/OFF; four-step gather ON/OFF loss comparison on every rank (`atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-3`), ownership, updates and DP replicas. Blockwise additionally checks readiness at direct convolution-weight reads. |
| Native MXFP8 flag behavior | Adam/Muon × layout × reuse: enabled cases train and check BF16 staging, copyback, scratch cleanup and DP equality of raw codes/dequantized values. Disabled cases check the existing storage/opt-in errors on these TE versions; they are not successful reuse-disabled training runs. |
| Checkpoint resume | Fixed-topology `torch_dist`: three steps → save → three more reference steps, then rebuild/load/resume. Exact model raw codes/dequantized values, FP32 masters, moments, scheduler and subsequent losses; both recipes, layouts and overlap settings. No old-container migration claim. |
| Explicit refresh | Existing nested-optimizer preparation/publication ordering and pending-gather handling; `zero_grad_buffer()` remains identical to main. |

The unit helpers do not directly compare TE's padded/swizzled scale arrays. The distributed unit snapshots are correctness checks, not overlap performance measurements.

### End-to-end comparisons

Within each recipe/layout: gather OFF and ON each run 200 steps; ON also saves at step 100 and resumes in a new process to step 200. The prefix retains the full 200-step LR schedule. This compares gather modes, not recipes or layouts against each other.

Ordinary DDP, 8 ranks, TP=PP=CP=ETP=1, DP=8, EP=2; four layers, hidden 512, eight experts/top-2 on alternating layers, sequence 512, MBS=1/GBS=8. Muon + Adam DistOpt, clip=1, cosine LR 1.5e-4 → 1e-5, warmup 10, seed 1234; overlap param gather and grad reduce enabled. The training probe adds no tensor reads, waits or collectives during steps. EOS uses SentencePiece/vocab 32,000; OCI uses DeepSeek-V3 HF/padded vocab 128,896, so hardware-to-hardware loss values are not a parity comparison.

| Hardware | Recipe | Muon layout | ON loss: first / last 20-step mean | Max OFF/ON loss diff | Max OFF/ON grad-norm diff | ON resume |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 / eos | blockwise | compact | 10.242427 / 7.175804 | 0 | 0 | Exact |
| H100 / eos | blockwise | padded | 10.242113 / 7.175243 | 0.00504732132 | 0.0558090210 | Exact |
| GB200 / oci-hsg | blockwise | compact | 11.671183 / 7.855774 | 0 | 0 | Exact |
| GB200 / oci-hsg | blockwise | padded | 11.671293 / 7.855762 | 0.00345230103 | 0.152322531 | Exact |
| GB200 / oci-hsg | MXFP8 | compact | 11.670957 / 7.855540 | 0 | 0 | Exact |
| GB200 / oci-hsg | MXFP8 | padded | 11.671160 / 7.855595 | 0.00357103348 | 0.0616674423 | Exact |

LR differences are zero for every OFF/ON pair. All six same-layout ON resumes have zero loss/grad-norm/LR difference over steps 101–200; all persisted checkpoint tensors match exactly (68 on EOS, 71 on OCI), including model, FP32 master and optimizer state. Iteration/scheduler/optimizer scalar state is also checked; RNG/non-tensor objects and serialization bytes are not included in this exact-state claim.

All three compact OFF/ON comparisons additionally match 57 named FP32 masters, 68 moment/momentum tensors and 13 high-precision model tensors exactly after reconstructing real DP shards. Quantized model storage is reported separately from OFF high-precision weights.

**The three padded OFF/ON strict comparisons failed; they are not reported as bitwise passes.** Training completed 200 steps; the jobs failed at the subsequent exact-state assertion. Those failures are preserved, while their independently executed resume comparisons passed. The loss windows show a short-run learning trend, not full convergence.

### Attribution against main

On GB200, padded MXFP8 was rerun on main `e30d863a6` and PR `238b019b9`, with gather OFF and ON separately: **main → PR has zero loss, grad-norm and LR difference at every one of 200 steps for either flag setting**. Main itself reproduces the same OFF/ON differences shown above.

Initial masters match exactly. Both versions move the same two BF16 router parameters between owners when FP8 changes the padded buffer grouping; Adam shard ranges stay identical. At step 2, every prepared gradient shard has identical bytes across OFF/ON, but the norm differs by one FP32 ULP. This supports sensitivity to the existing norm summation order with clipping. One router gradient hash already differs at step 1; its numerical magnitude was not decoded, so norm rounding is not claimed as the sole origin of all differences.

The diagnostic reads tensors only at initialization and before clipping in the first three steps. Its current-PR trajectories also match the original ordinary E2E trajectories exactly for all 200 steps. This main baseline covers **MXFP8 padded only**; blockwise's similar layout mechanism is a code-based inference, not a separately executed main/blockwise comparison.

<details>
<summary>Job IDs and reproducibility</summary>

Order: OFF full / ON full / ON prefix / ON resume. The marked failures are the post-training padded OFF/ON assertions.

- EOS blockwise compact: 6235662 / 6235679 / 6235682 / 6235704.
- EOS blockwise padded: 6235737 / 6235745 (failed) / 6235826 / 6235834.
- OCI blockwise compact: 7889352 / 7889449 / 7889496 / 7889577.
- OCI blockwise padded: 7889620 / 7889710 (failed) / 7889850 / 7889919.
- OCI MXFP8 compact: 7889783 / 7889835 / 7889959 / 7889987.
- OCI MXFP8 padded: 7889610 / 7889692 (failed) / 7889973 / 7890013.
- Main/current MXFP8 diagnostics: main OFF 7889984, main ON 7889985; PR OFF 7889986, PR ON 7889983.

Generated commands, manifests, every-step metrics, raw logs, source/image hashes and comparison reports are retained in the validation toolkit's `runtime/pr5479-compact-adam-distopt-20261012-e2e` on each cluster. Dataset/sample/shuffle cache checks match within every OFF/ON pair.

</details>

Local end-to-end runs use ordinary DDP and SlimPajama; GPU unit tests use synthetic batches. Neither run uses GTP or the Megatron functional-test runner. The compatibility images are NGC 26.04 (PyTorch 2.12.0a0/CUDA 13.2; TE 2.14 on H100, TE 2.16 on GB200). Rebased main uses a 26.09 CI image, so these results are separate from formal GPU CI.

The [public PR checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/5479/checks) remain the source for formal CI status. The two existing GTP tests remain `flaky_in_dev` and were not run locally. Functional golden values are unchanged.

+            value = torch.zeros(param.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=param.device)

+            if main is not None:
+                value.copy_(main.detach())

`_copy_main_params_to_model_params()` is the existing `Float16OptimizerWithFloat16Params` hook; the method name predates this change and pairs with `_copy_model_params_to_main_params()`.

`_copy_main_params_to_param_buffer()` has a different role: it is the DistributedOptimizer/MXFP8 staging helper that writes FP32 master shards into the DDP parameter buffer before parameter all-gather.

A compact non-DistOpt LayerWise child does not own that byte-sharded parameter buffer, so after the optimizer step it must use `_copy_main_params_to_model_params()` instead. The new branch also ensures FP8 parameters are written as `Q(bf16(master))` and skips parameters that will already be written by the LayerWise gather.

Here, `layout` means the mapping of each parameter into the contiguous DDP buffer: its start/end indices, bucket assignment, and the padding and shard boundaries used by that buffer.

For LayerWise-managed parameters, the padded layout places every whole parameter inside one DP shard, aligns parameter starts, and pads the shards to the same size. The compact layout instead uses the normal no-padding DDP ordering and keeps whole-parameter ownership in the LayerWise optimizer’s ping-pong assignment.

The layout always determines the grad-buffer placement. It also determines the param-buffer placement when that buffer uses DistributedOptimizer; compact non-DistOpt LayerWise buffers do not allocate a DDP param buffer.
